newsitem.title: USA: American Brands stock prices seen unleashed.
newsitem.headline: American Brands stock prices seen unleashed.

text.p: American Brands Inc shares are expected to sprint higher at the opening of trading on Tuesday after the company announced plans to spin off its U.K.-based Gallaher tobacco business.
"It's hot news," said Ronald Morrow, analyst at Rodman & Renshaw. "I think the stock will react positively this morning. My guess is it will move toward (a price of) 50."
Morrow said the stock's value has been stifled by the lingering association of its U.S.-based tobacco operations, American Tobacco Co, which was sold in 1994.
"I think they're very frustrated with the valuation of the stock," Morrow said.
He added that although Gallaher is dominant in Britain, it is a much smaller player in the rest of Europe. The spinoff unburdens the company from the slow growth limitations of Gallaher.
"It was a huge cash-flow generator for them, but they got no value for it," Morrow said.
He said the potential break-up value of American Brands shares have ranged from 60 to 75 a share when Gallaher is excluded, but said an accurate valuation was still to be determined.
American Brands settled Monday's trading at 44-12. Its 52-week range is a high of 47-7/8 to a low of 39-7/8.

The company sold its litigation risk when it sold its American Tobacco Co unit in 1994 to Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, so the move does not address any aspects of smoking-related lawsuits.

The operating environment for tobacco concerns in the United Kingdom is less problematic than in the United States, where thousands of lawsuits and a new level of regulatory oversight by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration confront the tobacco industry at every turn.
